renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: classifier_heatmap
  title: Cancer type by classifier
  description: |-
    Each cell is the probability one CUPPA classifier gives to one cancer type for a tumor, with the tumor as a row annotation. It answers whether the classifiers agree on a tissue of origin.
    How to read: a row that is high across the DNA and RNA classifiers is a call several independent feature families back. A row high in the combined column but low in the others rests on one family.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/cuppa/README.md
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: row_label
    row_annotation_cols:
    - sample

- component: table
  title: Classifier probabilities
  description: |-
    Each row is a cancer type for a tumor, with one probability column per classifier. It answers the exact score each classifier gave.
    How to read: sort by the combined column to see CUPPA's ranking and compare it with the feature classifiers.

- component: figure
  id: cancer_type_bar
  title: Probability of each cancer type
  description: |-
    Each bar is the probability one CUPPA classifier gives to a cancer type for a tumor, grouped by classifier. It answers which cancer type each feature family points to and how strongly.
    How to read: a cancer type with tall bars across the classifiers is a consistent call, and the combined classifier's top type is CUPPA's prediction. Disagreement between DNA and RNA classifiers means the call needs a second opinion. Use the classifier filter to read one at a time.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hartwigmedical/hmftools/master/cuppa/README.md
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: cancer_type
    y: probability
    color: classifier
    barmode: group
    labels:
      cancer_type: Cancer type
      probability: Probability
      classifier: Classifier

- component: interactive
  id: classifier_filter
  title: Classifier
  description: Restricts every tile to the chosen classifiers, such as the combined, DNA or RNA ones. It
    answers what one feature family alone predicts.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: classifier

- component: table
  id: prediction_table
  title: Tissue of origin probabilities
  description: |-
    Each row is a cancer type scored by one classifier for a tumor, with its probability, its rank within that classifier and a flag on the top call. It answers the ranking behind each prediction.
    How to read: filter to the combined classifier and sort by rank to read CUPPA's final prediction.
